gates.says: all 4 of this quiz's answerable readings held and each was taken over the question as it stands

recorded.prompt:q-hash: Read the whole lesson page, then this question. Using only what the page states, which option does the page decide is correct? Quote or cite the deciding passage.
recorded.outcome:q-hash: Python salts string hashes per process, so the weights change from run to run and the tie-break picks a different plan in each process: the opposite of what it was for.
recorded.prompt:q-workers: Read the whole lesson page, then this question. Using only what the page states, which option does the page decide is correct? Quote or cite the deciding passage.
recorded.outcome:q-workers: several workers with a seed still race: eight workers under a deterministic limit gave different plans, and only the experimental `interleave_search`, or one worker with a seed and a deterministic limit, repeated.
recorded.prompt:q-gpu-rerun: Read the whole lesson page, then this question. Using only what the page states, which option does the page decide is correct? Quote or cite the deciding passage.
recorded.outcome:q-gpu-rerun: cuOpt's default LP method is concurrent: PDLP, barrier and dual simplex race, and the first to finish answers.
recorded.prompt:q-fund: Read the whole lesson page, then this question. Using only what the page states, which option does the page decide is correct? Quote or cite the deciding passage.
recorded.outcome:q-fund: fund i in any year | a row, $\sum_{t \in T_i} x_{i,t} = 1$ (fund_i) ... "Fund in any year" is a sum over years, so no single bound can say it.
